sn1.24:1.1: These are some of the very few verses in the Pali Canon whose metre has not been identified.
sn1.24:2.2: The Pali readings _na mano saṁyatattamāgataṁ_ and _mano yatattam āgataṁ_ are both unsatisfactory. Both are unmetrical, the former because of the double initial short syllable, the latter because it has only eight syllables. Nor is the sense clear in either case. Chinese parallels offer a more satisfactory sense. SA 1281 has “only block (the mind’s) bad actions” (但遮其惡業), while SA-2 279 similarly has “only block bad thought-movement” (但遮惡覺觀). These seem to confirm the absence of _na_. Further, since both parallels have a term for “bad”, perhaps the original had _āgu taṁ_, misread in the Pali as _āgataṁ_. My translation is based on the supposition that the Pali is corrupt.
